briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Pain, Real Gains: Michigan Operators Find Wins as National Psychedelics and Rescheduling Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market is proving more resilient than the 24% wholesale tax headlines suggest, with new hospitality concepts, a legal win against surveillance overreach, and a GOP gubernatorial nominee now campaigning on tax relief. Nationally, the story is momentum: DEA is processing rescheduling protections, the FDA has a September 14 hearing on psychedelic therapeutics, and Compass Pathways keeps stacking wins toward a 2027 psilocybin launch.

local.text: A $4M dispensary-and-restaurant concept, Fields Cannary, is targeting a fall opening in Muskegon, pairing five licenses covering cultivation, processing, sales, on-site consumption and events under one roof. Co-owner Edgar Ramon and his partners hold five cannabis licenses covering cultivation, processing, sales, on-site consumption, and off-site events, along with a liquor license, and Fields Cannary represents a fully integrated cannabis hospitality model, combining retail, on-site consumption, dining, and event licensing under one business, testing whether a winery-style elevated experience can support higher price points.
Jars Cannabis wins removal of Madison Heights Flock camera — a rare, tangible win for an operator pushing back on local surveillance overreach that other Michigan retailers can now point to.

University of Michigan researchers have received federal funding for a study testing personalized marijuana coaching for adults with chronic lower back pain, a 12-month feasibility trial involving 80 adults in Michigan and California. It's another sign of cannabis research legitimacy landing on Michigan soil.

Michigan's GOP nominee for governor is promising to repeal or significantly roll back the marijuana wholesale tax hike if elected in November, arguing in his "Freedom Agenda" that the cannabis tax "drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections." That's now a live campaign issue operators can rally around heading into the fall.

The 24% wholesale tax keeps badly missing state targets — Michigan's 24% wholesale marijuana tax is still only bringing in a fraction of what state officials projected, generating about $37 million in Q2 2026 and roughly $34 million in Q1 against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter. The shortfall is fueling momentum for a Republican-introduced House Bill 6224 to repeal the 24% wholesale tax, characterizing it as an unnecessary burden on the industry — a real legislative path to relief.

national.text: The federal ban on hemp THC products that was supposed to take effect on Nov. 12 has been pushed back to Dec. 11 under a bill President Donald Trump signed last week, buying hemp brands and retailers a critical extra month to adapt or lobby for a permanent fix.

DEA's rescheduling process is moving into implementation: Marijuana Moment obtained a list of 26 questions that the Drug Enforcement Administration is sending to Colorado medical cannabis businesses that applied for federal protections in line with the Trump administration's rescheduling move. That's the clearest sign yet that federal protections tied to Schedule III are becoming operational, not just theoretical.

Mark your calendar: the FDA announced a public hearing on psychedelic therapeutic use scheduled for September 14, 2026 — a signal that the agency is building the institutional infrastructure for what may soon become a live approval docket. This follows finalized clinical trial guidance covering psilocybin, LSD and MDMA.

Compass Pathways keeps clearing hurdles toward market: commercial launch-readiness for COMP360 is on track for end of 2026, with launch expected in first half of 2027, built on 26-week findings in nearly 600 patients that build on the first Phase 3 trial's rapid onset and durable response to at least 6 months.

Fresh today: Compass Pathways has announced the recipients of its U.S. grant program aimed at developing training programs for healthcare providers involved in psychedelic treatments, specifically COMP360 psilocybin. It's the workforce buildout piece — getting clinicians ready before the approval clock even starts.
